prompt_arguments: local-full checkpoint:benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-2/tasks/t4/model.pt "This small transformer was built for a benchmark. Its input is a BOS token followed by exactly 4 tokens drawn from 6 symbols, and at the last position it outputs one symbol. The function it computes is deterministic and is published nowhere: work out from the model what it is. Then find which attention heads and MLP layers implement it. The model also contains components that play no part in the behaviour. Use the dataset task 'bench' with path 'benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-2/tasks/t4' (plus n and seed); its answers are the model's own outputs and the token strings are in its meta. Your predict(tokens, prompt) receives the full list of token ids including the BOS and must return the id of the output token. In verify_hypothesis give the circuit as a list of heads 'L.H' and MLP layers 'mlpL'. This model was trained by gradient descent, so it may be imperfect and its mechanism may be messy." budget=25 investigation=t4

final_message:
**Status: verified for the function and a five-component circuit, on local-full at full precision.** One caveat: the report header reads "partial / not verified · verified", most likely because the failed smaller-circuit attempt (V0002) stays in the record.

**The algorithm**

The output is a fixed lookup on the first and last input tokens; the two middle tokens are ignored. I found no simpler rule behind the table, so it is reported as a table.

| first \ last | fa | ku | fu | la | ma | vi |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **fa** | fa | ma | ku | ku | fu | la |
| **ku** | vi | ku | vi | la | fa | vi |
| **fu** | la | fu | vi | ma | fa | fa |
| **la** | ma | ma | fu | ku | la | la |
| **ma** | la | ma | vi | ku | fu | ma |
| **vi** | vi | ku | ma | fa | ku | vi |

**The circuit**

- **Circuit:** heads `0.0`, `1.0`, `1.1` and `mlp0`, `mlp1`.
- **Attention:** all four heads attend from the last position mostly to position 1, so the first token is carried to the output position in both layers (E0010, E0009).
- **MLPs:** both are necessary; ablating `mlp0` leaves 29% of the logit difference and `mlp1` leaves 24% (E0012). The answer only becomes decodable after layer 1 (E0015, exploratory).
- **Middle positions:** patching them restores less than 0.5% of the logit difference (E0009).
- **Outside the circuit:** only head `0.1`, and it is weak rather than inert. Ablating it keeps about 96.5% accuracy and 85% of the logit difference. No component measured as exactly zero, so `0.1` is the closest match to "plays no part".

**Verification numbers**

| Run | Circuit | Agreement with model | Circuit ablated (accuracy) | Rest ablated (accuracy) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0001 (seed 11) | `0.0`, `1.0`, `1.1`, `mlp0`, `mlp1` | 300/300 | 0.157 | 0.967 | verified, null controls passed |
| V0003 (seed 13) | same | 300/300 | 0.187 | 0.963 | verified, null controls passed |
| V0002 (seed 12) | without `0.0` | 300/300 | 0.153 | 0.577 | not verified |

V0002 shows head `0.0` cannot be dropped. Separately, the table matched the model on 72/72 designed prompts covering all 36 cells (E0005).

**Prediction record**

Eight predictions were pre-registered: 7 confirmed, 0 refuted, 1 inconclusive. The inconclusive one (E0017, "`mlp1` writes the answer") was my error: I registered a metric path that does not exist. The observed effects (`mlp1` 0.78, `mlp0` 0.76) do not separate the two MLPs, so what each MLP does individually is unresolved. I did not re-register it.

**What is not established**

- The head-to-MLP edges in the diagram are inferred from position-level patching and ablations, not from path patching.
- My first hand-reading of the table had two transcription errors, caught by E0003; the final table rests on E0005 and the verifications.

**Budget:** 17 of 25 experiments used, plus 3 verification runs.
